# Knowledge Space and Semiotics Instructions

Use these instructions when the material concerns visual grammar, knowledge-space terrain, colour, marker stability, semiotic sequencing, page navigation, satellite perspective, staged observation, or thought as terrain.

## Required Analysis

- Identify the visual/semiotic operation.
- Tag Book Part: Orientation / Grammar / Circuits / Futures.
- Tag EML Layer: Structural / Cognitive-Temporal / Agentic.
- Preserve distinctive phrases that name the visual operation.
- Decide whether the output is study, visual-language rule, diagram brief, circuit, lexicon, or book draft.

## Placement

| Output | Save location |
| --- | --- |
| Focused study | `03-Working/Knowledge-Space-Semiotics/` |
| Visual-language rule | `05-Assets/Visual-Language/` |
| Diagram brief | `05-Assets/Diagrams/` |
| Circuit | `05-Assets/Circuits/` |
| Stable definition | `06-Lexicon/Definitions/` |
| Book prose | `04-Book/Part-02-Grammar/` or `04-Book/Part-03-Circuits/` |

## Quality Bar

The visual language must make learning more navigable. If a marker, colour, line, or layout choice does not help the reader orient, return, compare, or revise, it is not yet functional grammar.
